newsitem.title: UK: UK power chiefs get 27 mln stg in pay-offs - paper.
newsitem.headline: UK power chiefs get 27 mln stg in pay-offs - paper.

text.p: A group of UK power industry executives scooped 26.9 million stg in pay-offs and compensation payments as a result of last year's takeovers and mergers in the electricity industry, the Guardian newspaper said Friday.
The scale of payments was revealed in documents filed at Companies House and analysed by the Guardian, the paper said.

Former Norweb Plc chairman Ken Harvey received a total package of nearly 3.0 million stg, including a last-minute pay rise of 377,000 stg before the company was bought by its neighbour, North West Water, the article said.
At Eastern Group, chairman John Devaney was paid more than 1.3 million stg for his share options when the company was bought last year, it said.
Large payments have also been made to small numbers of executives at Eastern Group, Seeboard, Manweb and South Wales Electricity.

Six regional electricity companies were bought last year as part of the wave of electricity takeovers. Midlands was acquired this year and neither it nor South Western Electricity has yet filed full accounts.
Total pay-offs will be much higher than the 26.9 million stg paid to date, once these two companies declare directors' remuneration, the paper said.
Northern Electricity and East Midlands Electricity are also set to change hands.

"The disclosures are certain to provoke a new political furore over greed by the privatised utilities which have already proved an acute embarrassment to (Prime Minister) John Major," the article said.
The huge payouts will infuriate trade unions in an industry which has seen 50,000 jobs cut in the six years since privatisation, it said.
